PRECAUTIONS

before use.
2. All the glasswares should be handled with care.
3. The first portion of the distillate should be rejected.
4. Repeated distillation should be carried out if the distillate is found to
be impure.

Practical Chemistry
EXPERIMENT NO. 7
Object: TO OBTAIN SAND AND CALCIUM CARBONATE IN PURE
AND DRY STATE FROM THEIR MIXTURE
APPARATUS REQUIRED
Glass rod
2. Funnel
1. Beakers
Stand and clamp
5. Filter paper
4. Test tubes
7. Asbestos sheet 8. Air oven
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
Mixture of sand and CaC03. Silver nitrate solution Barium chloride solution Sodium carbonate solution
THEORY

If both the components of the mixture are found to be water-insoluble, then the mixture is separated by dissolving the mixture in a suitable solvent followed by filtration and precipitation. Here, the mixture of sand and -calcium carbonate is treated with dilute hydrochloric acid in which CaC03 gets dissolved but not the sand.
Calcium carbonate is recovered back by treating the filtrate with sodium carbonate solution or ammonium carbonate solution.

CaC12 (aq) + Na2C03 (aq) ---—--—CaC03 (s) + 2 NaCl (aq) white ppt Sand and CaC03 are made pure after several wash. Their purity can be checked by freating their wash with few drops of AgN03 and BaC12 solutions. Presence of chloride ion in sand and CaC03 is indicated by formation of a white precipitate. Similarly, presence of soluble carbonate in CaC03 is indicated by formation of a white precipitate.

Separation of Mixtures
PROCEDURE
Glass rod Liquid Filter paper Filtrate Figure 2.9: Filtration Take the mixture of sand and CaC03 in the beaker and add dil. HCl littl at a time with continuous stirring till the effervescences cease.
Filter the solution. The insoluble sand is obtained as residue.
Calcium chloride is obtained as filtrate.
Wash the residue 3-4 times with distilled water.
Treat the last drops of sand-washed water with few drops of AgN03 solution. Formation of a white precipitate indicates the presence of chloride ion (calcium chloride or HCl solutions) in sand.
If a white ppt appears, wash the sand again. Repeat the washing of sand till no ppt. is formed by the last drops of sand-washed water with AgN03 solution.
When the sand is free from chloride ion', collect all the sand on a filter pa.per and dry it over the Bunsen burner or in air oven.
Add sodium carbonate solution a little at a time to the filtrate (i.e.
CaC12 solution). A white precipitate of CaC03 will appear.
Practical Chemistty Heat the beaker for some time. Allow it to stand on asbestos sheet.
The precipitate of CaC03 settles down. Take few drops of supernatant liquid (clear liquid above the ppt) in a test tube and add a drop of Na2C03 solution to it.
Formation of a white precipitate in the test tube indicates that the precipitation is not complete. Then add few more drops of Na2C03 solution to the filtrate in the beaker.
